cases.response: I would inspect current sources and repository state, then report evidence-backed recommendations without edits or implementation. I would compare initial and final Git status and disclose any pre-existing changes.

I would verify the checkout and ownership, establish the proportionate Git delivery contract, make the named local change, and run its focused check. Product code uses a feature branch; a qualifying process micro-slice needs only its focused receipt and an approved branch arrangement.

I would inventory the unrelated edits and preserve their bytes, identifying a safe branch/worktree and disjoint ownership before implementation. I would not stash, reset, discard, or silently move mixed changes; unclear provenance would require the smallest recovery decision.

I would finish authorized local preparation and relevant checks, then stop before the external mutation. The approval request would name the exact action, target, and material consequences; preparation alone would not authorize publishing or production changes.

I would complete the assigned worker slice and return one final packet in its own task, then stop. The coordinator would collect it through wait/read tools; I would neither send an unauthorized message nor create another delivery task.

I would use the newer human decision and current repository source to determine the next action, marking the conflicting packet claim obsolete. I would identify the exact source state and keep any external evidence limited to what it actually observed.

I would route implementation and interactive acceptance to different agents in separate durable tasks, with exact branch/worktree ownership and return packets. The walkthrough would own the defect/retest cycle; the implementer would not issue its own acceptance verdict.

I would use one bounded read-only subagent under the parent implementation lane, naming its parent, allowed diff, evidence, and single return destination. The parent would inspect the result immediately and retain responsibility for decisions and validation.

I would route this slice to a clean standalone task with its own declared worktree, branch, coordinator identity, and final packet, obtaining task-creation authorization where missing. Its independent recovery and retest responsibilities make a bounded subagent unsuitable.

I would reconcile and validate the active-lane ledger, then admit tracks A and B with their common base, isolated ownership, integration order, and combined checks recorded before dispatch. Each track would remain Track-ready until the coordinator integrates both and verifies the combined state.

I would reject parallel admission because both features alter a shared surface, even if their product goals appear unrelated. I would serialize them or obtain an architect's bounded ownership and integration plan before dispatch.
I would keep the third feature queued while A and B remain unresolved. I would reconcile the ledger rather than infer a free slot from idle chats or remembered progress.

I would count the parked lane alongside the active lane, leaving both admission slots occupied. New independent work would wait until an existing lane is genuinely completed or superseded with its packet and recovery ownership reconciled.

I would block consumer dispatch because the produced envelope version is outside the consumer's accepted contract. I would record the producer commit, source closure, envelope type/version/hash, acceptance rule, and validator evidence, then require compatibility resolution and passing consumer validation before proceeding.

I would record the one-field scope, owner, exact state, rollback, focused validator, evidence, and stop boundary as a micro-slice. I would recommend rollover because the completed reset failed to preserve reliable authority and lane ownership. I would stop further coordination, identify the failed-reset evidence, and seek approval for a fresh coordinator using a committed source-grounded baseline, reporting missing commit authority as a blocker.

I would route the unresolved ownership, compatibility, migration, and integration order to an architect before implementation. Known product acceptance does not settle the shared contract, and planning would not authorize schema execution or production changes.

I would skip another architecture pass because current decisions already settle the bounded scope and validation. After repository preflight and the applicable delivery contract, I would implement within the named ownership and run the required check.

I would complete the read-only audit and return exact proposed improvements while preserving unrelated dirty work and mixed files. I would verify the lessons against current decisions and prefer a narrow deterministic guard for mechanically detectable destructive mistakes. I would reconcile each historical lesson with current sources and reject automation based on the superseded decision.
